newsitem.title: USA: Hillsborough County, Fla., considers gasoline tax.
newsitem.headline: Hillsborough County, Fla., considers gasoline tax.

text.p: Transit authorities in Florida's Hillsborough County have asked the county comission to adopt a gasoline tax of at least 2 cents a gallon to offset an anticipated $4.5 million budget shortfall for bus services.
The commission was scheduled to vote on the proposal on Wednesday.

The Hillsborough Area Regional Transit Authority, with runs the bus system known as the HARTline, said that without the funding increase the authority would have to cut a third of its routes by August and lay off up to 100 employees.
Authority officials also said the county could face a lawsuit because the bus system cannot afford to provide services mandated by the Americans with Disabilities Act.
The shortfall was blamed on decreasing federal subsidies for the system, which relies on that funding plus state and local property taxes.
Transit officials and advocates for the handicapped said disabled and elderly riders make up 14 percent of county bus riders, and that 60 percent of bus trips are work-related.
About 73 percent of the system's riders either do not drive or have no access to cars.
